items.title: PG_CVE 1.1.1 Released
items.summary: We are pleased to announce the release 1.1.1 of PG_CVE, a lightweight tool designed to provide DBAs and system administrators with a clear, up-to-date overview of CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), known exploits, and release stability across PostgreSQL versions.Key Features & Highlights:Rapid tracking of security advisories and CVEs associated with specific PostgreSQL versions.Overview of release stability and patch information to assist DBAs with upgrade planning.Security context: integration of known exploit data for accurate vulnerability triage.Lightweight, standalone web interface for fast client-side navigation.Links & Resources:Live Interactive Demo: https://meob.github.io/PG_CVE/?version=15.8Source Code & Documentation: https://github.com/meob/PG_CVE

items.title: pg_fastload 1.0.0 released: parallel bulk loading for PostgreSQL
items.summary: pg_fastload 1.0.0 is a parallel bulk loader for PostgreSQL, 1.58x faster than the best pg_bulkload mode and 6.07x faster than COPY.It parallelises the loading pipeline across background workers while keeping the load inside a single transaction. It is a source-level fork of pg_bulkload 3.1.23, so control-file syntax, TYPE values, log format and WRITER modes are unchanged.Repository: github.com/yuansong/pg_fastloadRelease: pg_fastload v1.0.0License: BSD 3-Clause, with the upstream pg_bulkload copyright notices retainedThe problempg_bulkload and COPY both run the whole load in one backend: read, parse, form the tuple, write. On a 16-core machine that leaves 15 cores idle, and the parse step is usually the expensive one. For CSV it is a byte-at-a-time state machine followed by a type input function per column.How it worksThe load has four stages: read input, parse record and split fields, form the tuple, and insert. Stages 1-3 move to background workers; stage 4 stays serial in the backend that issued the load: one reader worker -> N parser workers -> leader writesDesign points that matter in practice:The input file is read exactly once. A single reader scans sequentially and hands chunks to the workers over shm_mq; the workers never open the file. Total read volume stays at 1x the file size, so the speedup does not invert once the data is larger than the page cache.It is still one transaction. No second connection, no early visibility of uncommitted rows, and a bad row aborts the whole load rather than leaving a worker-timing-dependent subset behind.13 conditions the parallel path cannot honour fall back automatically, with one INFO line saying why: FILTER and FORCE_NOT_NULL, explicit ENCODING, NOT NULL or CHECK constraints, PARSE_ERRORS tolerance, STDIN input, TUPLE and FUNCTION input, and others.The serial path itself was optimised. Records without quotes or CRs take a memchr bulk split instead of the byte-at-a-time loop.Progress reporting and exportEvery load and export publishes progress into a cluster-wide view, pgfastload.pg_fastload_progress: rows, bytes, rates and elapsed time. When a row total is known (a finite LIMIT, or a TABLE= export estimated from pg_class.reltuples), it also reports a percent and an ETA. Long loads are trackable from any session, or streamed as NOTICEs with PROGRESS_NOTICE=ON.Export logs additionally record the MVCC snapshot fingerprint (xmin/xmax/cid), so every output file is auditable back to the exact snapshot that produced it. pg_fastload_export() writes a table or any SELECT to CSV, BINARY or FIXED output.Results1 GiB TPC-H lineitem CSV, 7,375,042 rows, 16 vCPU, warm cache, WRITER=DIRECT, no indexes, median of 3 runs. Same file and same empty table for every row.configuration                         time     vs serial   vs COPY FROMPARALLEL=OFF                          5.81 s   1.00x       1.43xPARALLEL_WORKERS=4                    1.58 s   3.68x       5.27xdefault (15 workers)                  1.37 s   4.24x       6.07xreference: upstream pg_bulkload       6.98 sreference: COPY ... FROM              8.32 sreference: COPY into UNLOGGED table   7.51 sA full loader x writer-mode x format matrix (3 alternating rounds, medians):                                     CSV   BINARY    FIXEDupstream pg_bulkload BUFFERED       9.22     4.08     3.95upstream pg_bulkload DIRECT         6.98     1.62     1.59upstream pg_bulkload PARALLEL       6.63     1.39     1.42pg_fastload PARALLEL=OFF            5.84     1.58     1.63pg_fastload 8 workers               1.42     0.88     0.90pg_fastload default                 1.40     0.90     0.93COPY ... FROM                       8.34    (n/a)    (n/a)Upstream's own fastest writer mode is PARALLEL, about 13% ahead of its DIRECT, so the honest headline is 1.58x over the best upstream mode and 4.4-4.6x over its slowest, rather than the 2x+ that a DIRECT-only comparison suggests.Export shows the same effect in the other direction: 7.4M rows (1.13 GiB) take 4.08 s serial and 0.42 s with 15 workers, i.e. 9.33x server-side COPY TO. The export scan runs under one MVCC snapshot, serialized to the parallel workers, so an export under concurrent writes is consistent and reproducible.Method, fairness controls and the full result set (cold cache, fixed-length, export, historical tiers) are in docs/BENCHMARK.md in the repository, and all raw run logs ship with the release archive.Differences from upstream pg_bulkload 3.1.23Parallel CSV and parallel fixed-length loading, 4.7x and 1.6x over upstream's best mode. The serial path alone is 1.22x upstream with identical semantics.Load and export progress view with percent and ETA, plus NOTICE streaming.SKIP_INDEX=ON drops the target's secondary indexes inside the load transaction and prints the verbatim CREATE INDEX statements to re-create them, which recovers about half the load time on an indexed table.No spool busy-work on unindexed tables.Stage-level profiling build, and one branch for PostgreSQL 15 through 19

items.title: Apache Cloudberry 2.2.0 Released: PostgreSQL-Based MPP Database Moves to the PostgreSQL 14.10 Kernel
items.summary: The Apache Cloudberry (Incubating) community is pleased to announce the release of Apache Cloudberry 2.2.0, the latest version of its open-source massively parallel processing (MPP) database built on PostgreSQL for large-scale analytics and AI workloads.Following the 2.1.0 release, 2.2.0 continues the project's work on tracking upstream PostgreSQL, expanding the extension ecosystem, and broadening platform support.Key Enhancements in 2.2.0Tracking upstream PostgreSQL: The kernel moves from PostgreSQL 14.4 to 14.10, absorbing upstream optimizations, fixes, and hardening one minor release at a time.Security fixes: Dozens of upstream PostgreSQL CVE fixes are included, along with targeted cherry-picks of advisories published after 14.10.Six new extensions: diskquota, gp_stats_collector, gp_relsizes_stats, reject_partition_fullscan, try_convert, and yezzey.Query processing and observability: Interconnect statistics views, intra-segment parallel table scan in the ORCA optimizer, parallel Hash Full Join and Right Join, and multi-table join support for answering queries using materialized views (AQUMV).Platform coverage: Rocky Linux 8, 9, and 10 and Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 are supported and tested in CI. Ubuntu 20.04 is no longer supported.Packaging: Automated DEB and RPM builds for x86_64 and ARM64, and relocatable RPMs that allow multiple Cloudberry major versions to coexist on the same host.Apache Cloudberry 2.2.0 also includes coordinated releases of its ecosystem components:Cloudberry PXF: A new pxf_stat_activity view with pxf_cancel_backend and pxf_interrupt_backend functions, Java 17 support, and broader connector testing.Cloudberry Backup: A new gpbackman command for managing backups and gpbackup_exporter for Prometheus monitoring.Cloudberry Go Libs: The first release of cloudberry-go-libs as a versioned artifact for downstream components.Beyond the 2.x release line, the Cloudberry main branch has already been upgraded to the PostgreSQL 16 kernel, bringing features such as the MERGE command and SQL/JSON constructors to MPP workloads in a future major release.For the full list of changes, see the 2.2.0 changelog and the release announcement.DownloadApache Cloudberry 2.2.0 is available for download at: https://cloudberry.apache.org/releases.Get InvolvedThe community welcomes contributors and users interested in distributed PostgreSQL-based analytics systems.Website: https://cloudberry.apache.org/GitHub: https://github.com/apache/cloudberryIssue tracker: https://github.com/apache/cloudberry/issuesMailing list: https://lists.apache.org/list.html?dev@cloudberry.apache.orgAbout Apache CloudberryApache Cloudberry (Incubating) is an open-source Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) database for large-scale data analytics, derived from PostgreSQL and the last open-source version of Greenplum Database. It is designed to support both on-premise and cloud deployments, providing a scalable foundation for data warehousing and advanced analytics. The project is currently in incubation at the Apache Software Foundation.

items.title: Navicat Introduces Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL: Experience Enterprise-Grade PostgreSQL Database Management and Development
items.summary: Navicat, a leading provider of powerful database management and development software, is proud to unveil Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL, an innovative release that sets a new standard in PostgreSQL administration and development. Designed to simplify the complexities of managing on-premises and cloud-based PostgreSQL servers—including Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL, Amazon Redshift, Microsoft Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, and Fujitsu Enterprise Postgres—Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL introduces cutting-edge features and GUI enhancements that empower developers and database administrators to achieve unmatched efficiency and productivity.Key New Features in Navicat™ 18 for PostgreSQL•   AI Integration: Brings intelligent automation directly to the Data Editor and Table Designer. Users can populate, translate, and analyze columns in seconds with Fill with AI, or design PostgreSQL tables effortlessly using Ask AI, which defines columns and data types while automatically generating table summaries through Fill with Comment.•   Query Editing & Code Insight: Elevating code precision right inside the SQL Editor. Users can restructure complex queries effortlessly without breaking dependencies using Refactoring (Rename Symbol). Furthermore, the editor constantly analyzes scripts with Real-Time Error Detection to pinpoint syntax flaws, while Hover Info, Highlight Usages, and Go to Declaration uncover related items instantly.•   Data Masking: Secures sensitive production data for safe, compliant testing by transforming sensitive PostgreSQL records into realistic mock data. Supports industry-standard masking techniques including Substitution, Variance, Shuffling, Hashing, and Nulling.•   Model: Unifying conceptual design and physical structures. The new Hybrid Model maintains logical entities and physical constraints in a single workspace. Organizations can automatically enforce architectural consistency via Naming Standards & Glossary, while the Bulk Editor streamlines heavy updates across multiple tables simultaneously.•   Business Intelligence (BI) Features:o   Auto Tile: Dashboard components snap into a perfectly structured framework automatically, delivering a flawless, professional layout instantly without manual pixel-pushing.o   Parameters: Users can control data displays dynamically by defining global variables to filter, manipulate, and interact with key values on demand.o   Add-ons: Inject higher interactivity into reporting by easily configuring Page Navigation for seamless jumps between pages, and deploying Auto Refresh to pull live data automatically.•   Usability Enhancements: Experience an all-new Import Wizard designed for ultimate flexibility with live preview panels and support for Parquet files. Users can also modify multiple records freely across the grid using Batch Editing, and bypass sequential clicking via a dedicated Record Navigation side panel.•   Workspace Sync & History: Securely sync personal table profiles, connections, and UI color configurations directly to a private cloud account with Personal Profile Sync, and effortlessly track executed database commands via Session History.Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL is now available for download and purchase on the Navicat website at https://www.navicat.com/en/products/navicat-for-postgresql. Users can also download a 14-day fully functional free trial to experience the capabilities of Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL firsthand.To upgrade a previous version to Navicat 18 for PostgreSQL, please visit Navicat Customer Center.About NavicatNavicat develops leading database management and development software. Navicat for PostgreSQL provides an intuitive and powerful graphical user interface designed specifically for PostgreSQL database administration, development, data modeling, and business intelligence.
